limitations: PID and PGID reuse can cause false positive association; original process start times were not frozen.
This is a point-in-time view of OS-visible processes, not proof of global process absence.
Processes may exit or change identity between the cwd and ps snapshots; permissions may limit OS visibility.
Unobserved descendants that detached and changed parent, group, cwd and argv association can remain unknown.
Shared private-case cwd or argv associations do not uniquely establish ownership by this campaign.
Observer and its visible ancestors were excluded because their command source can contain campaign paths.
No harness started marker exists, so no campaign-owned harness temporary cwd was observed.
No conclusion about remote generation or billing follows from local process absence.
